guideTitle: The Best CPU Stands Under $75, from Rolling Bases to Desk Mounts
metaDescription: Spending up to $75 on a CPU stand buys formats beyond a basic rolling base. We compared six, including a charging cart and a standing-desk mount, on fit and features.
introParagraphs: Most rolling CPU stands cost under $30, so a $75 budget mainly opens up different formats: a two-tier cart with a charging station, and an under-desk holder that moves with a standing desk.
Fit still matters most. Width ranges here run from as narrow as 4.87 inches (Mount-It!) to larger stands for gaming cases, and the FLEXISPOT mount only works on dual-crossbeam standing desks.
Our comparison is based on published specifications and prices at the time of writing, not hands-on testing.

best-cpu-stands-under-75-1.summary: YOSE's basic computer tower stand, the lowest-priced option here.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-1.description:
The YOSE stand was the least expensive option here at the time of writing, at under $15.

Its listing summary gives no specifications, so check dimensions, adjustment range and whether it has wheels on the product page before buying.
cons: No specifications in the listing summary
best-cpu-stands-under-75-1.bestFor: A basic riser when price is the main concern.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-1.skipIf: You want listed features; the Hovadova adjustable states locking wheels for about $4 more.

best-cpu-stands-under-75-2.summary: Hovadova's adjustable stand with four 360-degree casters, locking wheels and tool-free setup.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-2.description:
The Hovadova adjustable stand adds locking wheels to the basics: four 360-degree casters, two of which lock, with tool-free setup. Hovadova says it lifts the tower away from dust, spills, carpet fibers and moisture.

It was under $17 at the time of writing. Dimensions aren't given in the listing summary.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-2.bestFor: Hard floors, where locking wheels stop drift.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-2.skipIf: You need side rails; the Hovadova Extra Large has them.

best-cpu-stands-under-75-3.badge: Best for Large Cases with Rails
best-cpu-stands-under-75-3.summary: Hovadova's extra-large rolling stand with side rails and four 360-degree wheels.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-3.description:
The Hovadova Extra Large suits bigger towers, with protective rails on both sides to keep the case from slipping off and four 360-degree wheels.

It costs more than Hovadova's standard stand at the time of writing, and dimensions aren't given in the listing summary.
cons: Costs more than the standard Hovadova
best-cpu-stands-under-75-3.skipIf: Your case is mid-size; the standard Hovadova is cheaper.

best-cpu-stands-under-75-4.summary: Mount-It!'s rolling stand adjusting 4.87 to 8.5 inches wide, with lockable wheels.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-4.description:
The Mount-It! fits narrower cases than most, adjusting from 4.87 to 8.5 inches wide, with lockable wheels and a ventilated design intended to improve airflow and reduce dust.

Its 8.5-inch maximum width rules out many larger gaming cases.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-4.skipIf: Your case is wider than 8.5 inches; the Hovadova Extra Large suits bigger towers.

best-cpu-stands-under-75-5.summary: A 2-tier, 16.9 x 11.4-inch PC cart adjustable from 19.7 to 31.5 inches tall, with a charging station.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-5.description:
The ZIIWIND is a two-tier PC cart rather than a low stand: 16.9 x 11.4 inches, with height adjustable from 19.7 to 31.5 inches, and a built-in charging station for your devices.

Lifting the tower well above the carpet keeps it clear of the pile. It was the most expensive option here at the time of writing and takes more space than a low stand.
pros: Lifts tower well off the floor
cons: Wheel details not stated in summary
best-cpu-stands-under-75-5.bestFor: A tower cart that doubles as a charging spot.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-5.skipIf: You only want the tower off the carpet; a low stand costs far less.

best-cpu-stands-under-75-6.badge: Best Under-Desk Mount for Standing Desks
best-cpu-stands-under-75-6.summary: FLEXISPOT's tool-free under-desk tower holder for dual-crossbeam standing desks.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-6.description:
The FLEXISPOT holder mounts under a standing desk so the tower rises and lowers with it, and it adjusts from 5.63 to 9.53 inches wide and 11.81 to 20.47 inches long for small to mid-size towers, with tool-free setup.

FLEXISPOT states it is for dual-crossbeam standing desks only, so confirm your desk frame before ordering. It was the most expensive option here at the time of writing.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-6.bestFor: Standing desks where the tower should move with the desktop.
best-cpu-stands-under-75-6.skipIf: Your desk has a single crossbar or no frame; a floor stand is the safer choice.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Rolling base, two-tier cart, or under-desk mount.
The Mount-It! suits slim cases; the Hovadova Extra Large suits bigger ones.
The FLEXISPOT requires a dual-crossbeam standing desk.
The Hovadova adjustable and Mount-It! list them.

faq.a: Not for a basic rolling stand; the extra budget buys carts or mounts.

faq.q: Will the FLEXISPOT fit my desk?
faq.a: Only dual-crossbeam standing desks, per FLEXISPOT.
The Hovadova adjustable and Mount-It! list locking wheels.
Most listings don't state one; check before loading a heavy tower.

bottomLine: For a simple rolling base, the Hovadova adjustable with locking wheels is enough, the Extra Large suits big cases, and the Mount-It! suits slim ones.
Spend more only for a different format: the ZIIWIND cart adds storage and charging, and the FLEXISPOT mount keeps a tower moving with a dual-crossbeam standing desk.
